engine._comment_adp: Sleeper is weighted higher because it is the ADP your leaguemates see inside the app they are drafting in. FFC still matters: it is the only source broken out by league size, and it supplies the per-player stdev.
engine._comment_position_value: Your thumb on the scale. 1.0 = trust the projections. Raise RB to lean earlier and harder on running backs than the math alone suggests.
engine._comment_market_ranked: Positions where the projection carries no usable signal, so the draft order within the position follows ADP instead. Kicker projections are pure noise; defence projections are not, and the backtest shows the engine already beats ADP there.
engine._comment_upside: Backtested to zero. The option-value model was a clean idea -- a bench player's downside is capped -- but 2023-2025 showed a monotonic decline as the weight rose (0.0->1852, 0.1->1841, 0.2->1818, 0.4->1768 pts). The UP column still displays; it just no longer steers the objective.
engine._comment_targets: Backtested off. Flat per-player penalties overwhelmed real value gaps -- the engine passed Kittle (VOR 65) for Pollard (VOR 58) to hit an RB target, then took a TE at VOR -24 in round 12. Depth demand now comes from starter_miss_rate, which the backtest values at +47 pts/season.

cache._comment: Short by design: it is draft season and ADP moves daily. Use --refresh to ignore these entirely.
